title: AtlasTrust - Private deployment security ops workshop
summary: Deep dive on private/VPC deployment security for AtlasTrust: network segmentation, ingress/egress controls, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logging, KMS key management, SOC2/ISO evidence mapping. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot in their dev VPC and provide an SCA checklist + hardened runbook.
topics: ingress patterns and load balancer placement
audit logs and retention for SOC2/ISO
data residency concerns and regional controls
next_steps: Redwood to share private deployment security brief + network reference diagram (by 2026-04-09)
AtlasTrust to provision dev VPC and invite Redwood service account (by 2026-04-13)
Schedule hands-on pilot kickoff with infra + security (target week of 2026-04-20)
Redwood SE to run latency/cost benchmark in pilot env and share spreadsheet
action_items: Olivia Grant; Send security brief + reference arch diagram; 2026-04-09
Daniel Ruiz; Provision dev VPC and service account for Redwood; 2026-04-13
Marcus Li; Prepare pilot test plan and benchmark spreadsheet; 2026-04-17
Aisha Khan; Share SOC2 in-scope controls and retention policy; 2026-04-12
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Grant: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Olivia from Redwood, AE on the account; with me is Marcus, our SE, and Jared joining for the runbook bits. How's that on your side?
[00:12] Priya Menon: Hi Olivia, yeah good thanks. I'm Priya — head of security at AtlasTrust — with Daniel and Aisha. We're trying to wrap our heads around how Redwood Private fits into our locked-down environment.
[00:22] Marcus Li: Great — quick agenda: network segmentation, ingress and egress patterns, key management, audit logs, and then pilot scope. We'll pause for questions as we go.
[00:33] Tom Becker: Quick ask up front — we need clear answers on whether any telemetry leaves our VPC by default, and what the control plane communication looks like.
[00:42] Jared Cole: Totally fair. For Private, the control plane can be put in a customer-managed VPC; there's an option for a proxy-only control path or fully air-gapped with one-time syncs depending on the package. We'll show both patterns.
[00:55] Daniel Ruiz: When you say proxy-only, is that an outbound-only connection? We can't accept inbound NAT from external IPs.
[01:06] Marcus Li: Yes, proxy-only uses an outbound egress tunnel to Redwood's control plane; all admin ops are initiated over an authenticated outbound connection and we keep the model artifacts in your environment. For air-gapped, we provide a signed bundle to apply manually — no outbound required after the bundle is installed.
[01:21] Aisha Khan: Okay, and from a compliance angle — SOC 2 — we need audit trails showing who invoked models and what input buckets were used. How detailed are your logs?
[01:33] Olivia Grant: We can emit audit logs that include request metadata: calling user or service principal, model version, token counts, and request/response hashes. For private deployments the logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog/S3/CloudWatch. Note: we don't store plaintext customer data unless configured for debugging.
[01:48] Priya Menon: Can we control retention? Our policy is 365 days for request metadata, 30 days for raw payloads unless approved.
[01:57] Marcus Li: Retention is configurable; by default we keep minimal metadata for 90 days — but in Private you can configure the logging agent to ship to your S3 with lifecycle rules. We'll add this to the checklist.
[02:08] Tom Becker: Network segmentation question — do you require a dedicated subnet per model pool or can we colocate on shared infra within our VPC?
[02:17] Jared Cole: Recommended is a dedicated subnet per Redis/KV-cache and one for GPU workers, that gives us security boundaries and clear flow logs. You can colocate, but that'll increase blast radius and make firewall rules more complex.
[02:29] Daniel Ruiz: How about LB placement — we want the LB internal-only with mTLS to the workers. Do you support client certs or mTLS termination?
[02:39] Marcus Li: Yes, internal LBs are supported. In Private we recommend terminating mTLS at the LB and using mutual auth between internal services. Redwood's runtime supports TLS mutual auth for node-to-node and we can plug into your PKI for cert rotation or use the KMS-backed cert manager.
[02:52] Priya Menon: KMS — we currently use a cloud KMS (HSM backed) and an internal key admin process. We can't have Redwood hold keys. How do you integrate?
[03:03] Olivia Grant: For Private we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM — we never require root keys. The service can request encrypted material and use a local key wrapper encrypted with your KMS. If you go fully air-gapped, keys stay with you and we only get wrapped keys during the initial install.
[03:17] Aisha Khan: Do you support key rotation without downtime? That's a hard requirement for us.
[03:24] Marcus Li: Yes — hot rotation is supported, it's a rolling rewrap. We'll run through our rotation playbook in the pilot and show the certificate/key rotation steps in staging.
[03:34] Daniel Ruiz: Egress control — what external endpoints does Redwood need to call? We have very strict allow-lists.
[03:41] Jared Cole: For the proxy model it's a small set of outbound endpoints for telemetry and control, all over TLS and authenticated. We'll provide an allow-list. For air-gapped there's zero egress after install. Also model downloads can be proxied through your internal artifact repo if desired.
[03:56] Priya Menon: We also have data residency requirements — some PII must remain in EU regions. Can we pin model execution to eu-west-1 workers?
[04:04] Marcus Li: Absolutely — you can configure region affinity and Redwood will schedule workers in your specified region. For Private, that's controlled entirely by your infra. We'll add region pinning instructions to the deployment guide.
[04:16] Olivia Grant: One practical caveat: some optimized kernels have region-specific builds. If you require a custom kernel set, we'll coordinate a build and test cycle.
[04:26] Tom Becker: On RBAC and SSO — our SAML identity provider is IdentiCorp (SAML 2.0). We need role-based controls that mirror our internal roles: dev, infra, security, compliance. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[04:39] Marcus Li: We support RBAC mappings to SAML/OIDC groups and can sync groups to roles: viewer, operator, model-deployer, auditor. You can create custom roles too. For Private, the control plane will accept your IdP assertions and map roles automatically.
[04:52] Aisha Khan: Are there separate auditing hooks for admin vs. service-account activity?
[04:57] Jared Cole: Yes — admin actions (config changes, rollouts, key unwrapping) are logged with user identity; service accounts are tagged and we emit the principal id. Both are available in the audit stream with different retention controls.
[05:09] Priya Menon: What about network level logging — VPC flow logs, etc. Do you recommend capturing those and correlating with your request logs?
[05:17] Marcus Li: Definitely; we recommend centralizing VPC flow logs, host-level process telemetry if you have it, and Redwood audit logs into your SIEM. That aids forensic investigations and SOC2 evidence collection.
[05:28] Daniel Ruiz: Any known gotchas with autoscaling and ephemeral worker IP churn causing firewall rule churn? We prefer using NAT gateway with egress proxy to avoid changing firewall rules on scaling events.
[05:41] Marcus Li: Right — best practice is to egress through a NAT/proxy with static outbound IPs or an egress gateway. Redwood also supports an internal egress-proxy sidecar pattern that funnels all outbound to a fixed interface, so your allow-list remains stable.
[05:54] Tom Becker: Do you have recommended firewall rules at the subnet level?
[05:59] Jared Cole: Yes — we'll provide a hardened baseline: deny by default, allow control-plane outbounds only to pinned addresses, allow internal ports for metrics and KV caches, and restrict API access to the internal LB via mTLS. We'll drop that into the runbook.
[06:12] Priya Menon: For SOC2 we need evidence that admin privileges are separated and change control exists. How do you support separation of duties?
[06:21] Olivia Grant: We support RBAC, approval workflows for rollouts, and can integrate with your ticketing system for change approvals. We also keep immutable audit logs with tamper-evidence (signed log streams) that you can ingest into your retention store.
[06:33] Aisha Khan: Tamper-evidence — is that using append-only storage with signing? We need to map this to CC6/CC7 controls.
[06:40] Marcus Li: We sign log entries with a rotation-protected key and provide a verification tool. We can include a mapping matrix for SOC 2/ISO controls showing where logs and controls meet each requirement.
[06:52] Daniel Ruiz: Performance question: if we enable request-level logging and full payload capture for debugging, what's the perf cost? Our SLAs are strict.
[07:02] Marcus Li: Capturing full payloads will increase latency slightly and throughput overhead — we'd recommend toggling full payload capture to a sampling mode or only enabling it in pre-prod. Metadata-level logs have negligible impact. We'll show benchmark numbers in the pilot.
[07:16] Priya Menon: On DLP — can Redwood redact certain sensitive fields before logs leave our environment?
[07:23] Jared Cole: Yes — the log pipeline supports configurable redaction rules and regex filters before shipping. For Private you can run redaction locally and only send sanitized metadata.
[07:33] Tom Becker: If we want to run on-prem with no internet, what's the supported maintenance cadence? We need patching, security updates — how do you deliver those?
[07:43] Olivia Grant: For air-gapped/on-prem we provide signed update bundles on a quarterly or on-demand cadence. You apply them via a signed installer. We also offer a remote-assisted patch window where an engineer can guide you through the steps without persistent access.
[07:56] Aisha Khan: Is there an attestation artifact after patching — like a signed manifest we can store?
[08:02] Marcus Li: Yes, every bundle includes a signed manifest and checksum; we can also provide an SBOM for the deployed components for your software supply chain records.
[08:14] Daniel Ruiz: Let's talk threat model: if a worker is compromised, what controls reduce lateral movement?
[08:21] Jared Cole: We recommend strict micro-segmentation, host hardening, and ephemeral workers with minimal privileges. The runtime enforces process-level controls and user namespaces; KV caches and credentials are isolated per tenant and are rotated frequently.
[08:34] Priya Menon: Does the runtime run as root anywhere?
[08:37] Marcus Li: No, by default the runtime runs under a constrained user and uses seccomp and capability dropping. Some ops require elevated privileges during initial device mapping, but that's in the install window and documented.
[08:49] Tom Becker: For our internal change control we want a demo of the role mapping flow — creating an IdP group and seeing role change propagate. Can you show that in the pilot?
[08:58] Olivia Grant: Yes, pilot plan will include SAML group mapping demo, RBAC change test, and key rotation. Marcus will lead the technical sessions.
[09:06] Marcus Li: I'll prepare a step-by-step playbook and a short screencast for your infra team.
[09:11] Aisha Khan: One last thing — data residency again: if we pin to eu-west-1, can we also ensure backups/snapshots do not cross region?
[09:19] Marcus Li: Yes — snapshot configuration is under your control in Private; we'll provide guardrails to ensure backups are stored in the same region and provide checks in the deploy pipeline.
[09:29] Priya Menon: This is helpful. For the SOC2 mapping, can you provide a pre-filled evidence map for CC6/CC7/CC8?
[09:36] Olivia Grant: We have a SOC2 evidence pack template; we'll populate a mapping for AtlasTrust and return it with the runbook.
[09:44] Daniel Ruiz: Are there any compatibility issues with our internal artifact repo (Nexus)? We want to pull model artifacts through it.
[09:51] Jared Cole: Supported — our artifact puller can authenticate to Nexus and pull model tarballs. We'll need a read-only service account for the pilot.
[09:59] Tom Becker: Okay, next steps and responsibilities?
[10:03] Olivia Grant: I'll share the security brief and reference VPC diagram by Friday (2026-04-09). Marcus will send the pilot plan and benchmark spreadsheet by next Thursday. Daniel to provision dev VPC and service account by 2026-04-13. Aisha to share SOC2 in-scope docs by 2026-04-12.
[10:19] Priya Menon: Sounds good. Anything else on vendor lock-in or fallback strategies?
[10:24] Marcus Li: You can export model checkpoints and configs; we use standard formats so switching/handoff is straightforward. Plus we provide export scripts in the runbook.
[10:33] Olivia Grant: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links: security brief (https://docs.redwood.ai/atlastrust-security-brief.pdf), pilot plan doc (link to be shared), and the allow-list spreadsheet.
[10:46] Priya Menon: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:49] Call ended with brief informal sign-offs and a note to set the pilot kickoff calendar invite.
